In production enterprise clusters, worker nodes must be drained for kernel upgrades, hardware fails unexpectedly, and workloads need CPU/RAM adjustments without downtime. If you treat a Virtual Machine like an ephemeral container and simply terminate it during node maintenance, you will cause an unexpected service outage for your end users. In this sixth and final installment of our OpenShift Virtualization (CNV) Zero to Hero series, we tackle Day-2 operations: Mastering Zero-Downtime Live Migration. articles.title: Pick Queue Versus Cron for Scheduled Support Data Cleanup Needs
articles.excerpt: Short answer: Pick cron for a bounded, repeatable sweep that can rediscover eligible rows; pick a queue when each cleanup item needs its own due time, retry history, or operator-visible state. The dec…
articles.body: Short answer: Pick cron for a bounded, repeatable sweep that can rediscover eligible rows; pick a queue when each cleanup item needs its own due time, retry history, or operator-visible state. The deciding constraint is time semantics, not whether the job happens every hour. A queue is the better fit when each cleanup item has its own deadline, retry history, or operator-visible state; cron is the better fit when one trusted clock should periodically discover a bounded batch. The deciding constraint is time semantics, not whether the job happens every hour. I build support automation in Python, and this distinction matters for a mundane task: removing expired conversation attachments and compacting stale metadata without holding a web request open.

articles.title: Part 5: Enterprise Backup & Disaster Recovery with OADP & NooBaa
articles.excerpt: Virtual Machines, however, are massive stateful engines. If you take a naive snapshot of a running virtual machine while an active database is processing write transactions in RAM, your restored VM wi…
articles.body: Backing up stateless microservices in Kubernetes is relatively straightforward: export your GitOps manifests, and redeploy. Virtual Machines, however, are massive stateful engines. If you take a naive snapshot of a running virtual machine while an active database is processing write transactions in RAM, your restored VM will likely boot into a corrupted filesystem, broken journal logs, or lost transactions (the dreaded "Crash-Consistent" state). To achieve true enterprise-grade Application Consistency , we must coordinate three distinct layers: The guest operating system's internal filesystem memory buffers. The hypervisor virtualization engine (KubeVirt). The underlying storage array CSI snapshot controller.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.excerpt: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.body: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life.

The latest electric SUVs, “coming soon” tiny trucks, lifestyle trucks, modular trucks, etc. Companies like Slate, TELO, and countless others have generated plenty of excitement, even if many of them still have everything left to prove. Don’t get me wrong – I hope they succeed. We need more affordable electric vehicles.
